statci Architecture

Source: ARCHITECTURE.md

statci brings software-engineering-grade continuous integration, static methodological verification, probabilistic calibration fuzzing, manuscript-to-code auditing, and adversarial sensitivity testing to statistical R pipelines and Quarto/RMarkdown manuscripts.

1. High-Level Module Map

Unified Status Algebra

Every verification subsystem emits structured S3 objects whose overall status belongs to a three-level ordered lattice:

pass<warn<fail\text{pass} < \text{warn} < \text{fail}

Across components and unified reports (statci_report()), statuses compose monotonically via max\max: any single fail elevates the parent section and overall report to fail; otherwise any warn elevates to warn; otherwise pass. CI quality gates (statci_check_gate()) translate this lattice directly into deterministic pass/error behavior for GitHub Actions.

2. Pillar 1: AST-Based Statistical Linter

2.1 Parsing Strategy for .R, .qmd, and .Rmd

Rather than applying fragile regexes to raw text, statci parses code into full R parse trees via base::parse(keep.source = TRUE), converts the parse table to XML via xmlparsedata::xml_parse_data(), and queries syntactic structure with XPath (xml2::xml_find_all()).

For .qmd and .Rmd documents, extract_r_chunks() identifies fenced R code chunks (```{r ...} / ```{R ...}) and builds a blank-line-preserving document projection:

  1. Every non-R-chunk line (YAML frontmatter, markdown prose, fence delimiters, non-R chunks) is replaced with an empty line "".
  2. Code lines inside R chunks stay at their exact 1-based original file line numbers.
  3. A parallel line-to-chunk map records the chunk label ({r label} or Quarto #| label: ...) for each code line.

This design solves two classic notebook-linting pitfalls simultaneously: - Zero line-offset drift: xmlparsedata line1/col1 attributes match original .qmd/.Rmd line numbers directly. - Cross-chunk scope awareness: A set.seed(42) in an early setup chunk properly satisfies downstream stochastic calls in later chunks, while a scale(df) in chunk 1 before a train/test split in chunk 2 is caught as cross-chunk data leakage.

If the combined document projection fails to parse (e.g., an intentional syntax error in one chunk), the parser gracefully falls back to per-chunk parsing with exact line offsets so valid chunks are still linted and the invalid chunk yields a parse_error diagnostic.

2.2 Inline Suppressions

Authors can silence intentional exceptions using standard line comments: - # statci-ignore — suppresses all rules on that line. - # statci-ignore: rule_a, rule_b — suppresses specific rule IDs on that line. - # statci-ignore-next-line / # statci-ignore-next-line: rule_a — suppresses the immediately following line.

2.3 Extensible Rule Engine & Built-in Rules

Rules are statci_rule S3 objects stored in a package registry environment (.statci_rule_registry). Users inspect rules via list_stat_rules(), register custom AST rules via register_stat_rule(new_stat_rule(...)), and filter rules per invocation via rules / exclude_rules.

statci ships 20 built-in statistical & methodological lint rules:

# Rule ID Severity Category Methodological Hazard Caught
1 unseeded_randomness error reproducibility Top-level stochastic calls (rnorm, sample, boot, kmeans, etc.) without prior set.seed(), withr::with_seed(), RNGkind(), or enclosing seed wrapper
2 unsafe_parallel_rng error parallel_rng mclapply/parLapply/foreach %dopar%/future_* without L’Ecuyer-CMRG, clusterSetRNGStream, %dorng%/doRNG, or future.seed
3 duplicate_parallel_seed error parallel_rng Constant set.seed(42) inside loops or parallel workers producing identical duplicate Monte Carlo draws
4 preprocessing_before_split error data_leakage Global scale(), prcomp(), preProcess(), mice(), etc. executed on a dataset before train/test splitting
5 in_sample_prediction_eval warning data_leakage Evaluating RMSE/MAE/AUC/MSE on training-set predictions rather than held-out test/CV data
6 uncentered_mlm_interaction warning modeling Fixed-effect interactions (*, :) in lmer/glmer/lme/glmmTMB/brm using raw predictors with no centering call, naming suffix, or prior centering definition
7 silent_listwise_mismatch warning modeling Comparing models with differing predictor sets via anova(), AIC(), BIC(), or lrtest() on an unharmonized dataset without na.omit/complete.cases/drop_na/na.action = na.fail
8 silent_factor_drop warning modeling as.numeric()/as.integer() applied directly to a factor variable (coercing level indices), or passing a subset()/filter() data frame to modeling/contrast functions without droplevels()/fct_drop()
9 silent_na_coercion warning data_integrity Unchecked as.numeric()/as.integer() coercion of character/parsed strings without anyNA()/is.na() checks
10 unverified_merge_cardinality warning data_integrity dplyr::*_join() or base merge() without relationship = or nrow() guards against silent many-to-many row duplication
11 missing_drop_false_matrix warning data_integrity 2D matrix/array subsetting (X[, cols], X[idx, ]) lacking drop = FALSE, silently collapsing 1-row/1-column matrices to atomic vectors
12 implicit_na_rm_masking info data_integrity Unconditional na.rm = TRUE in summary statistics without nearby missingness inspection (is.na(), anyNA(), complete.cases())
13 equality_on_float warning numerics Exact == / != on floating-point literals or computed continuous expressions instead of all.equal(), near(), or tolerance checks
14 unadjusted_multiple_testing warning inference Hypothesis tests (t.test, cor.test, wilcox.test, lm p-values, etc.) run inside loops/applies without p.adjust() or multiple-testing correction in scope
15 stepwise_selection_unvalidated warning modeling In-sample step()/MASS::stepAIC()/regsubsets() without cross-validation or holdout validation
16 missing_convergence_check warning modeling Iterative models (lmer, glmer, optim, nlminb, glmmTMB) fitted without programmatic AST checks for convergence or isSingular()
17 global_seed_override_in_fn warning reproducibility Calling bare set.seed() inside reusable functions or \(...) lambdas without restoring .Random.seed via on.exit() or withr::local_seed()/with_seed()
18 short_logical_literal warning hygiene Using mutable T/F symbols as logical literals/arguments instead of reserved TRUE/FALSE (ignoring user-bound numeric variables like T <- 100)
19 cor_without_use_arg info modeling Calling cor() or cov() without an explicit use = missing-data policy
20 absolute_path_in_script warning reproducibility Hardcoded machine-specific absolute paths (/Users/..., /home/..., C:\..., ~/...) in file I/O or setwd() calls

2.4 Incremental Git-Diff Pull-Request Linting (stat_lint_diff())

stat_lint_diff() parses unified diffs (diff_text or read-only git diff --unified=0 against strictly validated Git refs via validate_git_ref()), enforces repository root confinement on every modified file path, executes full-file AST linting (so upstream context like set.seed() is preserved), and emits only findings landing on added or modified lines alongside diff_meta$n_suppressed_untouched.

3. Pillar 2: Estimator Calibration & Fuzzing Harness

Deterministic unit tests cannot detect biased custom estimators, anti-conservative standard errors, broken MCMC/posterior samplers, or parallel RNG stream collisions. statci implements finite-sample probabilistic verification accounting explicitly for Monte Carlo standard error (MCSE).

3.1 Parameter Recovery, Coverage, SE Ratio & Type-I Error (audit_estimator())

Given a user dgp function, an estimator function (returning either a named list or a standard R model object lm/glm/lmerMod/htest), and true_params, audit_estimator() runs MtotalM_{\text{total}} replications inside a locally scoped RNG state (withr::local_seed()), capturing errors, convergence failures, and singular fits cleanly. Let MM be the number of converged replications:

  1. Bias Check: Biaŝ=θ̂‾−θ,MCSEbias=sθ̂M,zbias=|Biaŝ|MCSEbias\widehat{\text{Bias}} = \bar{\hat\theta} - \theta, \qquad \text{MCSE}_{\text{bias}} = \frac{s_{\hat\theta}}{\sqrt{M}}, \qquad z_{\text{bias}} = \frac{|\widehat{\text{Bias}}|}{\text{MCSE}_{\text{bias}}}
    • fail if zbias>τbiasz_{\text{bias}} > \tau_{\text{bias}} (default 3.03.0) and |Biaŝ|>10−8|\widehat{\text{Bias}}| > 10^{-8};
    • warn if 2.0<zbias≤τbias2.0 < z_{\text{bias}} \le \tau_{\text{bias}};
    • pass otherwise.
  2. Interval Coverage Calibration (Exact Clopper-Pearson Binomial Bounds): For nominal level 1−α1 - \alpha and k=∑m=1M𝟏(θ∈[L̂m,Ûm])k = \sum_{m=1}^M \mathbf{1}(\theta \in [\hat L_m, \hat U_m]), ĉ=k/M\hat c = k/M with MCSEcov=ĉ(1−ĉ)/M\text{MCSE}_{\text{cov}} = \sqrt{\hat c(1-\hat c)/M}. Exact two-sided binomial testing (stats::binom.test(k, M, p = 1 - alpha)) yields exact p-value pcovp_{\text{cov}} and Clopper-Pearson interval [cL,cU][c_L, c_U]:
    • fail if pcov<αmcp_{\text{cov}} < \alpha_{\text{mc}} (default 0.01) and |ĉ−(1−α)|>0.015|\hat c - (1-\alpha)| > 0.015;
    • warn if pcov<0.05p_{\text{cov}} < 0.05;
    • pass otherwise.
  3. Model SE vs. Empirical SE Ratio: Let R=SÊ¯/sθ̂R = \overline{\widehat{\text{SE}}} / s_{\hat\theta} with asymptotic MCSE MCSER≈R/2(M−1)\text{MCSE}_R \approx R / \sqrt{2(M-1)}. Using configurable target bounds [Rmin,Rmax][R_{\min}, R_{\max}] (default [0.85, 1.15]):
    • fail if the 95% MC interval [R−1.96MCSER,R+1.96MCSER][R - 1.96\,\text{MCSE}_R,\, R + 1.96\,\text{MCSE}_R] lies completely outside [Rmin,Rmax][R_{\min}, R_{\max}];
    • warn if the point ratio RR lies outside [Rmin,Rmax][R_{\min}, R_{\max}] and |R−1|/MCSER>2.0|R - 1| / \text{MCSE}_R > 2.0;
    • pass otherwise.
  4. Type-I Error Calibration (Null DGP or Null Parameters): Under null_dgp (or any parameter where θj=0\theta_j = 0), let k0=∑m=1M0𝟏(pm≤α)k_0 = \sum_{m=1}^{M_0} \mathbf{1}(p_m \le \alpha) and α̂=k0/M0\hat\alpha = k_0 / M_0. Using stats::binom.test(k_0, M_0, p = alpha):
    • fail if pbinom<αmcp_{\text{binom}} < \alpha_{\text{mc}} and (α̂>α\hat\alpha > \alpha or α̂<α/4\hat\alpha < \alpha/4);
    • warn if pbinom<0.05p_{\text{binom}} < 0.05;
    • pass otherwise.
  5. Convergence & Singularity Auditing: Tracks error rate, non-convergence rate, and singular-fit rate (lme4::isSingular() or returned singular = TRUE) against configurable thresholds (max_fail_rate, warn_fail_rate, max_singular_rate).

3.2 Simulation-Based Calibration (audit_sbc())

Implements Talts et al. (2018): for s=1,…,Ss = 1, \dots, S, draws θ̃s∼p(θ)\tilde\theta_s \sim p(\theta), simulates ỹs∼p(y∣θ̃s)\tilde y_s \sim p(y \mid \tilde\theta_s), obtains LL posterior draws {θs(l)}l=1L\{\theta_s^{(l)}\}_{l=1}^L, and computes rank statistic: rs=∑l=1L𝟏(θs(l)<θ̃s)∈{0,1,…,L}r_s = \sum_{l=1}^L \mathbf{1}\!\left(\theta_s^{(l)} < \tilde\theta_s\right) \in \{0, 1, \dots, L\} (with randomized tie-breaking for discrete ties). Under a calibrated posterior sampler, rs∼DiscreteUniform{0,…,L}r_s \sim \text{DiscreteUniform}\{0, \dots, L\}. audit_sbc() bins ranks into BB equal-probability bins and evaluates uniformity via both Pearson’s χ2\chi^2 test (chisq.test) and a Kolmogorov-Smirnov test on us=(rs+0.5)/(L+1)u_s = (r_s + 0.5)/(L + 1), alongside central 50% and 90% posterior interval coverage.

3.3 Parallel RNG Invariance (check_parallel_rng() & statci_parallel_apply())

A subtle R parallelization trap is that standard parallel::mclapply(..., mc.set.seed = TRUE) or clusterSetRNGStream(cl) assigns one stream per worker, so running with cores = 1 vs cores = 2 vs cores = 4 produces different Monte Carlo realizations!

  • statci_parallel_apply(X, FUN, cores, seed) solves this by pre-generating one independent "L'Ecuyer-CMRG" stream per task i∈{1,…,|X|}i \in \{1, \dots, |X|\} via parallel::nextRNGStream(), assigning .Random.seed inside each task before invoking FUN(X[[i]]). Output is mathematically bit-for-bit identical across any number of cores on macOS, Linux, and Windows (using PSOCK clusters with strict on.exit(stopCluster(cl)) hygiene).
  • check_parallel_rng() executes a user-supplied parallel runner(cores, seed) (or fun via statci_parallel_apply) across core counts (default c(1L, 2L), honoring CRAN’s 2-core limit) and verifies exact numerical equivalence (identical() / all.equal(tolerance = 0)), failing immediately on any core-count discrepancy.

4. Pillar 3: Manuscript-to-Code Consistency Auditor (audit_manuscript())

4.1 Document Parsing & Tagging Grammar

audit_manuscript() strips YAML frontmatter and fenced code blocks (preserving exact line numbers) and extracts statistical claims from prose in two modes:

  1. Explicitly Tagged Claims (Zero-Ambiguity Binding):
    • HTML comment anchor preceding text: <!-- statci: model=fit1 term=x1 -->
    • Inline Quarto span: [b = 0.42, SE = 0.11, p = .003]{.statci model="fit1" term="x1"}
    • Model-level anchor (for NN, R2R^2, AIC, BIC): <!-- statci: model=fit1 -->
  2. Automatic Prose Extraction (Untagged Matching): Recognizes standard APA / statistical typography (including markdown italics *b*, *p*, LaTeX inline math $b = 0.42$, Unicode minus −, and leading-dot decimals .003):
    • Point estimates (b, B, beta, β, est, estimate, OR, coef)
    • Standard errors (SE, S.E.)
    • Confidence intervals (95% CI [L, U], CI (L, U), 95% CI: L to U)
    • p-values (p = .003, p < .001, p <= .05, p > .05)
    • Sample sizes (N = 250, n = 250)
    • Test & fit statistics (t(df) = ..., z = ..., r = ..., R^2 = ..., AIC = ...)

4.2 Uniform Model Artifact Extraction

Accepts a named list of R models, a single model, an .rds file, or a directory of .rds files. Supports lm, glm, lmerMod/glmerMod/lmerModLmerTest, htest, and tidy data.frame/tibble tables.

4.3 Rounding-Aware Verification Algebra

For any numeric claim reported with dd decimal places (e.g., 0.42 has d=2d = 2): - Let δ=0.5×10−d+ϵextra\delta = 0.5 \times 10^{-d} + \epsilon_{\text{extra}} be the rounding half-unit. - Sign Flip (fail): sign(reported)≠sign(actual)\text{sign}(\text{reported}) \ne \text{sign}(\text{actual}) while |actual|>δ|\text{actual}| > \delta and reported≠0\text{reported} \ne 0. - Exact Rounding Match (pass): |actual−reported|≤δ+10−9|\text{actual} - \text{reported}| \le \delta + 10^{-9}. - Rounding Discrepancy (warn): δ<|actual−reported|≤1.5×10−d+ϵextra\delta < |\text{actual} - \text{reported}| \le 1.5 \times 10^{-d} + \epsilon_{\text{extra}} (off by 1 unit in the final decimal place, e.g., truncation instead of half-to-even rounding). - Value Mismatch (fail): |actual−reported|>1.5×10−d+ϵextra|\text{actual} - \text{reported}| > 1.5 \times 10^{-d} + \epsilon_{\text{extra}}. - Inequality p-values (p < c / p <= c / p > c): Verified directly as exact boolean inequalities against the model’s unrounded p.value. - Sample size (N): Exact integer equality against nobs(model).

5. Pillar 4: Adversarial Sensitivity & Robustness Battery (audit_sensitivity())

Given data, fit_fn(df), and extract_fn(fit), audit_sensitivity() automatically executes four orthogonal perturbation suites around the baseline fit:

  1. Outlier Winsorization: Clamps continuous non-binary, non-cluster numeric predictors/outcomes to [qp,q1−p][q_p, q_{1-p}] (default p∈{0.01,0.05}p \in \{0.01, 0.05\}).
  2. Leave-One-Cluster-Out (LOCO) / Leave-One-Out (LOO) Influence: Sequentially omits each cluster (cluster_col) or observation (capped at max_loo_units, prioritizing high-leverage rows for linear models when subsampling), reporting maximum shift, most influential unit, jackknife SE, and any single-unit sign reversal.
  3. Missingness & Imputation Stress Tests: Evaluates observed-data missingness handling (if NAs already exist) plus controlled MCAR perturbation at configured rates (default 5% and 10%) contrasting complete-case deletion against median/mean imputation.
  4. Nonparametric Bootstrap Stability: Performs cluster bootstrap (resampling whole clusters when cluster_col is given) or row bootstrap, reporting bootstrap mean, SE, percentile CI, sign consistency rate, and refit convergence rate.

Each perturbation records baseline estimate, perturbed estimate, absolute shift, relative % change, sign-flip indicator, and pass/warn/fail classification.

5.1 Multiverse Specification-Curve Auditor (audit_multiverse())

audit_multiverse() evaluates a pipeline across the full Cartesian grid of named analytical decisions (guarded by max_specs), sorting converged specifications by point estimate and computing:

  • Overall median, interquartile range (IQR), IQR / |median| spread ratio, sign consistency, and proportion statistically significant (p≤αp \le \alpha);
  • One-way per-fork variance decomposition (η2=SSbetween/SStotal\eta^2 = \text{SS}_{\text{between}} / \text{SS}_{\text{total}} and median range across each fork’s choices) identifying the top driver of estimate dispersion (most_influential_fork);
  • Publication-ready two-panel plot() combining the sorted specification curve (point estimates and confidence intervals colored by significance) above a decision-choice indicator matrix.

6. Pillar 5: Unified Audit Report & GitHub Actions Integration

  • statci_report() aggregates lint, estimator calibration, SBC, power-curve, parallel RNG, manuscript, sensitivity, and multiverse objects into a single statci_report S3 object with unified summary metrics and session metadata.
  • statci_check_gate() enforces CI exit gates (fail_on = "fail" or "warn"), throwing a structured error in non-interactive CI runs when thresholds are breached.
  • render_statci_report() generates:
    • Self-contained, offline-capable HTML5 audit dashboards (safely escaped with htmltools),
    • GitHub-Flavored Markdown reports suitable for $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY and PR reviews,
    • Machine-readable JSON artifacts (via jsonlite).
  • use_statci_github_action() writes a ready-to-run .github/workflows/statci.yaml workflow installing dependencies, running statci audits, publishing Markdown summaries to GitHub Actions, and uploading HTML reports as workflow artifacts.
